A1.1:
- Strict A1.1 style.
- Use very high-frequency daily vocabulary.
- Prefer present tense only.
- Use one clear clause.
- Keep sentence length around 5 to 8 words.
- Use very concrete real-life situations.
A1.2:
- A1.2 style.
- Prefer present tense.
- Use one clear clause, with an occasional simple fixed phrase.
- Keep sentence length around 6 to 9 words.
- Use practical daily contexts such as home, shopping, transport, and family.
A2.1:
- A2.1 style.
- Mostly present tense; Perfekt is allowed when natural.
- Use one clause or two short natural clauses.
- Keep sentence length around 7 to 11 words.
- Use realistic everyday contexts, not textbook nonsense.
A2.2:
- A2.2 style.
- Present and Perfekt are both acceptable.
- Use one to two short clauses.
- Keep sentence length around 8 to 12 words.
- Allow slightly richer real-life detail and simple connectors.
B1.1:
- B1.1 style.
- Use natural practical German.
- One to two clauses with clear connectors.
- Keep sentence length around 9 to 14 words.
- Add believable context from normal life, work, study, or travel.
B1.2:
- B1.2 style.
- Use natural modern German with mild complexity.
- One to two clauses, sometimes with a smoother connector.
- Keep sentence length around 10 to 16 words.
- Make examples feel like something a real person would say.
DEFAULT: - {level} learner style.\n- Keep the language clear, natural, practical, and teacher-friendly.\n- Prefer believable real-world usage over abstract or artificial examples.
